tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

10	failed run leaves the previous output exactly as it was.
11	"""

14	import csv

16	import json
17	import os

19	import subprocess

28	class InputVerificationError(RuntimeError):
29	    """An input differs from what the collection manifest recorded."""

32	def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
33	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
34	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
35	        while block := f.read(1 << 20):
36	            digest.update(block)
37	    return digest.hexdigest()

44	def tool_revision() -> str:
45	    """The git commit this pipeline ran from, marked dirty if uncommitted."""
46	    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
47	    try:
48	        head = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=here, capture_output=True,
49	                              text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
50	        dirty = subprocess.run(["git", "status", "--porcelain", "--", "."], cwd=here.parent,
51	                               capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
52	    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
53	        return "unknown"
54	    return head + ("+dirty" if dirty else "")

57	class Lake:
58	    def __init__(self, root: Path | str | None = None) -> None:
59	        chosen = root or os.environ.get("ALMANAC_FOOD_DATA") or DEFAULT_ROOT
60	        self.root = Path(chosen).expanduser().resolve()
61	
62	    @property
63	    def manifests(self) -> Path:
64	        return self.root / "manifests"
65	
66	    @property
67	    def canonical_root(self) -> Path:
68	        return self.root / "processed" / "canonical"
69	
70	    def extracted(self, namespace: str) -> Path:
71	        return self.root / "processed" / "extracted" / namespace
72	
73	    def canonical(self, namespace: str) -> Path:
74	        return self.canonical_root / namespace
75	
76	    @property
77	    def union(self) -> Path:
78	        return self.root / "processed" / "union"
79	
80	    @property
81	    def bundle(self) -> Path:
82	        return self.root / "build" / "almanac.sqlite"
83	
84	    def manifest(self, name: str) -> dict:
85	        return json.loads((self.manifests / f"{name}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
86	
87	    def source_dir(self, manifest_name: str) -> Path:
88	        return self.root / self.manifest(manifest_name)["local_path"]
89	
90	    def verify_inputs(self, manifest_name: str, filenames: Iterable[str]) -> list[dict]:
91	        """Checksums every input against the collection manifest before it is read."""
92	        manifest = self.manifest(manifest_name)
93	        recorded = {entry["filename"]: entry for entry in manifest["files"]}
94	        base = self.root / manifest["local_path"]
95	        verified = []
96	        for name in filenames:
97	            entry = recorded.get(name)
98	            if entry is None:
99	                raise InputVerificationError(f"{name} is not recorded in manifests/{manifest_name}.json")
100	            path = base / name
101	            if not path.is_file():
102	                raise InputVerificationError(f"{path} is missing")
103	            actual = sha256_file(path)
104	            if actual != entry["sha256"]:
105	                raise InputVerificationError(
106	                    f"{path}: sha256 {actual} differs from the manifest's {entry['sha256']}")
107	            verified.append({"file": str(path.relative_to(self.root)), "sha256": actual})
108	        return verified

111	@contextmanager
112	def staged_directory(final: Path) -> Iterator[Path]:
113	    """Yields an empty scratch directory that replaces `final` only on success."""
114	    final = Path(final)
115	    final.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
116	    scratch = final.with_name(f".{final.name}.partial")
117	    if scratch.exists():
118	        shutil.rmtree(scratch)
119	    scratch.mkdir()
120	    try:
121	        yield scratch
122	    except BaseException:
123	        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
124	        raise
125	    retired = final.with_name(f".{final.name}.retired")
126	    if retired.exists():
127	        shutil.rmtree(retired)
128	    if final.exists():
129	        final.rename(retired)
130	    scratch.rename(final)
131	    shutil.rmtree(retired, ignore_errors=True)

130	def load(directory: Path | str = DICTIONARY_DIR) -> Dictionary:
131	    directory = Path(directory)
132	    problems: list[str] = []
133	
134	    nutrients: dict[str, Nutrient] = {}
135	    for r in _read(directory, "nutrients.csv"):
136	        if r["nutrient_id"] in nutrients:
137	            problems.append(f"nutrients.csv: duplicate nutrient_id {r['nutrient_id']}")
138	        if not r["unit"]:
139	            problems.append(f"nutrients.csv[{r['nutrient_id']}]: unit is empty")
140	        nutrients[r["nutrient_id"]] = Nutrient(r["nutrient_id"], r["infoods_tag"], r["name"],
141	                                               r["unit"], r["description"])
142	
143	    qualifiers: dict[str, Qualifier] = {}
144	    for r in _read(directory, "qualifiers.csv"):
145	        where = f"qualifiers.csv[{r['qualifier']}]"
146	        if r["qualifier"] in qualifiers:
147	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
148	        if r["amount_rule"] not in ("null", "required"):
149	            problems.append(f"{where}: amount_rule must be null or required")
150	        qualifiers[r["qualifier"]] = Qualifier(
151	            r["qualifier"], _flag(r["has_quantity"], where, problems),
152	            _flag(r["directly_observed"], where, problems), r["amount_rule"], r["description"])
153	
154	    groups: dict[str, LicenceGroup] = {}
155	    for r in _read(directory, "licence_groups.csv"):
156	        where = f"licence_groups.csv[{r['licence_group']}]"
157	        if r["licence_group"] in groups:
158	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
159	        groups[r["licence_group"]] = LicenceGroup(r["licence_group"], r["name"],
160	                                                  _flag(r["shippable"], where, problems),
161	                                                  r["description"])
162	
163	    sources: dict[str, Source] = {}
164	    for r in _read(directory, "sources.csv"):
165	        where = f"sources.csv[{r['namespace']}]"
166	        if r["namespace"] in sources:
167	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
168	        if r["licence_group"] not in groups:
169	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown licence group {r['licence_group']!r}")
170	        sources[r["namespace"]] = Source(r["namespace"], r["dataset_id"], r["name"], r["release"],
171	                                         r["licence"], r["licence_group"], r["attribution"], r["url"])
172	
173	    mappings: list[Mapping] = []
174	    seen_ids: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
175	    seen_priorities: set[tuple[str, str, int]] = set()
176	    for r in _read(directory, "nutrient_map.csv"):
177	        where = f"nutrient_map.csv[{r['source']} {r['source_nutrient_id']}]"
178	        try:
179	            priority = int(r["priority"])
180	        except ValueError:
181	            problems.append(f"{where}: priority {r['priority']!r} is not an integer")
182	            continue
183	        m = Mapping(r["source"], r["source_nutrient_id"], r["source_nutrient_name"], r["source_unit"],
184	                    r["nutrient_id"], priority, r["unit_conversion"],
185	                    r["numeric_qualifier_override"], r["notes"])
186	        if m.source not in sources:
187	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown source")
188	        nutrient = nutrients.get(m.nutrient_id)
189	        if nutrient is None:
190	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown nutrient {m.nutrient_id!r}")
191	        if (m.source, m.source_nutrient_id) in seen_ids:
192	            problems.append(f"{where}: mapped twice")
193	        seen_ids.add((m.source, m.source_nutrient_id))
194	        if (m.source, m.nutrient_id, m.priority) in seen_priorities:
195	            problems.append(f"{where}: priority {priority} repeated for {m.nutrient_id}")
196	        seen_priorities.add((m.source, m.nutrient_id, m.priority))
197	        if priority < 1:
198	            problems.append(f"{where}: priority must be 1 or more")
199	        if m.numeric_qualifier_override and m.numeric_qualifier_override not in qualifiers:
200	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown override qualifier {m.numeric_qualifier_override!r}")
201	        if m.unit_conversion not in UNIT_CONVERSIONS:
202	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown unit_conversion {m.unit_conversion!r}")
203	        elif nutrient is not None:
204	            conversion = UNIT_CONVERSIONS[m.unit_conversion]
205	            source_unit, canonical_unit = m.source_unit.lower(), nutrient.unit.lower()
206	            if conversion is None and source_unit != canonical_unit:
207	                problems.append(f"{where}: source unit {m.source_unit!r} is not {nutrient.unit!r} "
208	                                "and no unit_conversion is given")
209	            if conversion is not None and conversion != (source_unit, canonical_unit):
210	                problems.append(f"{where}: {m.unit_conversion} converts {conversion[0]} to "
211	                                f"{conversion[1]}, not {source_unit} to {canonical_unit}")
212	        mappings.append(m)
213	
214	    derivations: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
215	    for r in _read(directory, "derivation_qualifiers.csv"):
216	        where = f"derivation_qualifiers.csv[{r['source']} {r['code']!r}]"
217	        if r["source"] not in sources:
218	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown source")
219	        if r["qualifier"] not in qualifiers:
220	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown qualifier {r['qualifier']!r}")
221	        if (r["source"], r["code"]) in derivations:
222	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
223	        derivations[(r["source"], r["code"])] = r["qualifier"]
224	
225	    tokens: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
226	    for r in _read(directory, "value_tokens.csv"):
227	        where = f"value_tokens.csv[{r['source']} {r['token']!r}]"
228	        if r["source"] not in sources:
229	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown source")
230	        qualifier = qualifiers.get(r["qualifier"])
231	        if qualifier is None:
232	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown qualifier {r['qualifier']!r}")
233	        elif qualifier.amount_rule != "null":
234	            # A token carries no number. Mapping one to a qualifier that needs an
235	            # amount would force the pipeline to invent one — which is the bug.
236	            problems.append(f"{where}: a token may only map to a qualifier with no amount, "
237	                            f"not {r['qualifier']!r}")
238	        if r["token"] != r["token"].strip() or not r["token"]:
239	            problems.append(f"{where}: token must be non-empty and trimmed")
240	        if (r["source"], r["token"]) in tokens:
241	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
242	        tokens[(r["source"], r["token"])] = r["qualifier"]
243	
244	    if problems:
245	        raise DictionaryError(f"{len(problems)} problem(s) in {directory}:\n  " + "\n  ".join(problems))
246	    return Dictionary(nutrients, qualifiers, groups, sources, tuple(mappings), derivations, tokens,
247	                      _digest(directory))

1	"""Turning one source cell into (amount, qualifier) — Processing Design v0.1 §2.
2	
3	The most consequential bug available in this project is a one-line type
4	coercion that turns CoFID's `Tr` or `N` into 0. Every source goes through
5	`qualify`, which has no path from a non-numeric cell to a number other than
6	an explicit, bounded `< x`.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import math
11	import re
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from typing import Any, Sequence
14	
15	KJ_PER_KCAL = 4.184  # thermochemical calorie
16	_DECIMAL = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?")
17	
18	
19	class UnrecognisedValue(ValueError):
20	    """A cell no rule covers. The stage fails rather than guess."""
21	
22	
23	class NegativeAmount(UnrecognisedValue):
24	    """A published number below zero — not a quantity. Never stored, never clamped to 0.
25	
26	    Source modules may catch this one case, emit no row, and record the cell in
27	    their manifest's notes.rejected_values (README "Qualifying a value").
28	    """
29	
30	
31	@dataclass(frozen=True)
32	class Qualified:
33	    amount: float | None
34	    qualifier: str
35	
36	
37	def parse_decimal(text: str, *, decimal_comma: bool = False) -> float | None:
38	    """A plain finite decimal, or None. Never NaN, never infinity, never a token."""
39	    s = text.strip()
40	    if decimal_comma and s.count(",") == 1 and "." not in s:
41	        s = s.replace(",", ".")
42	    if not _DECIMAL.fullmatch(s):
43	        return None
44	    number = float(s)
45	    return number if math.isfinite(number) else None
46	
47	
48	def qualify(cell: str, *, tokens: dict[str, str], numeric_override: str = "",
49	            derivation_qualifier: str = "", decimal_comma: bool = False,
50	            bound_prefix: str = "") -> Qualified:
51	    """The README's seven-step rule, in order. Blank cells never get here."""
52	    text = cell.strip()
53	    if not text:
54	        raise UnrecognisedValue("blank cell reached qualify(); a blank cell produces no row")
55	    if text in tokens:
56	        return Qualified(None, tokens[text])
57	    if bound_prefix and text.startswith(bound_prefix):
58	        bound = parse_decimal(text[len(bound_prefix):], decimal_comma=decimal_comma)
59	        if bound is None or bound <= 0:
60	            raise UnrecognisedValue(f"{cell!r}: a bound must be a positive number")
61	        return Qualified(bound, "below_loq")
62	    number = parse_decimal(text, decimal_comma=decimal_comma)
63	    if number is None:
64	        raise UnrecognisedValue(f"{cell!r} is neither a number nor a known token")
65	    if number < 0:
66	        raise NegativeAmount(f"{cell!r}: a nutrient amount cannot be negative")
67	    if number == 0:
68	        return Qualified(0.0, "zero_reported")
69	    if numeric_override:
70	        return Qualified(number, numeric_override)
71	    if derivation_qualifier:
72	        return Qualified(number, derivation_qualifier)
73	    return Qualified(number, "measured")
74	
75	
76	def convert(amount: float | None, conversion: str) -> float | None:
77	    if amount is None or not conversion:
78	        return amount
79	    if conversion == "kj_to_kcal":
80	        return amount / KJ_PER_KCAL
81	    raise ValueError(f"unknown unit conversion {conversion!r}")
82	
83	
84	def select(candidates: Sequence[tuple[int, Qualified, Any]]) -> tuple[int, Qualified, Any] | None:
85	    """One value where several source columns feed one canonical nutrient.
86	
87	    `candidates` are (priority, Qualified, payload). The lowest priority that
88	    carries a quantity wins; if none does, the lowest priority's marker is
89	    kept rather than dropped.
90	    """
91	    ordered = sorted(candidates, key=lambda c: c[0])
92	    for candidate in ordered:
93	        if candidate[1].qualifier != "not_analysed":
94	            return candidate
95	    return ordered[0] if ordered else None

72	        if f.licence_group != dictionary.group_of(f.namespace):
73	            problems.append(f"{where}: licence group {f.licence_group!r}, but sources.csv says "
74	                            f"{dictionary.group_of(f.namespace)!r}")
75	        if f.food_ref in foods_by_ref:
76	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate food_ref")
77	        foods_by_ref[f.food_ref] = f
78	
79	    primaries: Counter[str] = Counter()
80	    seen_names: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
81	    for n in names:
82	        where = f"name {n.food_ref}/{n.language}"
83	        if n.food_ref not in foods_by_ref:
84	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown food")
85	        if not _LANGUAGE.fullmatch(n.language):
86	            problems.append(f"{where}: language must be a lower-case ISO 639 code")
87	        if not n.name.strip():
88	            problems.append(f"{where}: empty name")
89	        if (n.food_ref, n.language) in seen_names:
90	            problems.append(f"{where}: two names in one language")
91	        seen_names.add((n.food_ref, n.language))
92	        primaries[n.food_ref] += n.is_primary
93	    for ref in foods_by_ref:
94	        if primaries[ref] != 1:
95	            problems.append(f"food {ref}: {primaries[ref]} primary names, needs exactly 1")
96	
97	    seen_values: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
98	    for v in values:
99	        where = f"value {v.food_ref}/{v.nutrient_id}/{v.basis}"
100	        food = foods_by_ref.get(v.food_ref)
101	        if food is None:
102	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown food")
103	            continue
104	        if v.nutrient_id not in dictionary.nutrients:
105	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown nutrient")
106	        if v.basis not in BASES:
107	            problems.append(f"{where}: basis must be one of {BASES}")
108	        qualifier = dictionary.qualifiers.get(v.qualifier)
109	        if qualifier is None:
110	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown qualifier {v.qualifier!r}")
111	        elif qualifier.amount_rule == "null" and v.amount is not None:
112	            problems.append(f"{where}: {v.qualifier} must have no amount, got {v.amount!r} "
113	                            "— a token is never coerced to a number")
114	        elif qualifier.amount_rule == "required" and v.amount is None:
115	            problems.append(f"{where}: {v.qualifier} requires an amount")
116	        if v.amount is not None and (not math.isfinite(v.amount) or v.amount < 0):
117	            problems.append(f"{where}: amount {v.amount!r} is not a finite non-negative number")
118	        if v.qualifier == "zero_reported" and v.amount != 0:
119	            problems.append(f"{where}: zero_reported with amount {v.amount!r}")
120	        # Independent of the qualifier logic: only a cell that says zero may become 0.
121	        if v.amount == 0 and parse_decimal(v.source_value, decimal_comma=True) != 0:
122	            problems.append(f"{where}: amount 0 from source cell {v.source_value!r} "
123	                            "— only an explicit zero may become 0")
124	        if not v.source_value.strip():
125	            problems.append(f"{where}: source_value is empty")
126	        if not v.source_nutrient_id or not v.source_unit:
127	            problems.append(f"{where}: source_nutrient_id and source_unit are required")
128	        if v.licence_group != food.licence_group:
129	            problems.append(f"{where}: licence group {v.licence_group!r} differs from its food's "
130	                            f"{food.licence_group!r}")
131	        key = (v.food_ref, v.nutrient_id, v.basis)
132	        if key in seen_values:
133	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate value")
134	        seen_values.add(key)
135	
136	    return problems
137

1	"""Reading and writing canonical row sets (README "Canonical format").
2	
3	The same three files describe processed/canonical/{namespace}/ and
4	processed/union/; only the manifest differs.
5	"""
6	from __future__ import annotations
7	
8	from collections import Counter
9	from pathlib import Path
10	from typing import Iterable, Sequence
11	
12	from .dictionary import Dictionary
13	from .lake import (read_csv, read_json, sha256_file, staged_directory, tool_revision, utc_now,
14	                   write_csv, write_json)
15	from .model import Food, FoodName, Value, validate
16	
17	ROW_FILES = ("foods.csv", "food_names.csv", "values.csv")
18	FOOD_COLUMNS = ["food_ref", "namespace", "local_id", "licence_group", "food_group_code",
19	                "food_group_name", "source_record"]
20	NAME_COLUMNS = ["food_ref", "language", "name", "is_primary"]
21	VALUE_COLUMNS = ["food_ref", "nutrient_id", "basis", "amount", "qualifier", "confidence",
22	                 "source_value", "source_nutrient_id", "source_unit", "licence_group"]
23	
24	
25	class CanonicalError(ValueError):
26	    """A row set breaks the contract. Nothing is written."""
27	
28	
29	def format_amount(amount: float | None) -> str:
30	    return "" if amount is None else repr(float(amount))
31	
32	
33	def parse_amount(text: str) -> float | None:
34	    return None if text == "" else float(text)
35	
36	
37	def raise_if_invalid(problems: Sequence[str], what: str) -> None:
38	    if problems:
39	        shown = "\n  ".join(problems[:30])
40	        more = f"\n  … and {len(problems) - 30} more" if len(problems) > 30 else ""
41	        raise CanonicalError(f"{what}: {len(problems)} problem(s)\n  {shown}{more}")
42	
43	
44	def counts(foods: Sequence[Food], names: Sequence[FoodName], values: Sequence[Value]) -> dict:
45	    return {
46	        "foods": len(foods),
47	        "names": len(names),
48	        "values": len(values),
49	        "values_by_nutrient": dict(sorted(Counter(v.nutrient_id for v in values).items())),
50	        "values_by_qualifier": dict(sorted(Counter(v.qualifier for v in values).items())),
51	        "values_by_basis": dict(sorted(Counter(v.basis for v in values).items())),
52	        "foods_without_values": len({f.food_ref for f in foods} - {v.food_ref for v in values}),
53	    }
54	
55	
56	def write_rows(directory: Path, foods: Iterable[Food], names: Iterable[FoodName],
57	               values: Iterable[Value]) -> dict[str, str]:
58	    """Writes the three row files in key order; returns their SHA-256s."""
59	    write_csv(directory / "foods.csv", FOOD_COLUMNS, (
60	        [f.food_ref, f.namespace, f.local_id, f.licence_group, f.food_group_code,
61	         f.food_group_name, f.source_record]
62	        for f in sorted(foods, key=lambda f: f.food_ref)))
63	    write_csv(directory / "food_names.csv", NAME_COLUMNS, (
64	        [n.food_ref, n.language, n.name, "1" if n.is_primary else "0"]
65	        for n in sorted(names, key=lambda n: (n.food_ref, n.language))))
66	    write_csv(directory / "values.csv", VALUE_COLUMNS, (
67	        [v.food_ref, v.nutrient_id, v.basis, format_amount(v.amount), v.qualifier, v.confidence,
68	         v.source_value, v.source_nutrient_id, v.source_unit, v.licence_group]
69	        for v in sorted(values, key=lambda v: (v.food_ref, v.nutrient_id, v.basis))))
70	    return {name: sha256_file(directory / name) for name in ROW_FILES}
71	
72	
73	def write_canonical(out_dir: Path, *, namespace: str, foods: Iterable[Food],
74	                    names: Iterable[FoodName], values: Iterable[Value], dictionary: Dictionary,
75	                    inputs: list[dict], notes: dict | None = None) -> dict:
76	    """Validates, then replaces `out_dir`. An invalid set leaves the old output untouched."""
77	    foods, names, values = list(foods), list(names), list(values)
78	    raise_if_invalid(validate(foods, names, values, dictionary, namespace=namespace),
79	                     f"canonical/{namespace}")
80	    source = dictionary.sources[namespace]
81	    with staged_directory(out_dir) as scratch:
82	        manifest = {
83	            "stage": "canonical",
84	            "namespace": namespace,
85	            "dataset_id": source.dataset_id,
86	            "release": source.release,
87	            "licence_group": source.licence_group,
88	            "dictionary_sha256": dictionary.sha256,
89	            "generated_at": utc_now(),
90	            "tool_revision": tool_revision(),
91	            "inputs": inputs,
92	            "outputs": write_rows(scratch, foods, names, values),
93	            "counts": counts(foods, names, values),
94	            "notes": notes or {},
95	        }
96	        write_json(scratch / "manifest.json", manifest)
97	    return manifest
98	
99	
100	def read_rows(directory: Path) -> tuple[list[Food], list[FoodName], list[Value]]:
101	    foods = []
102	    for r in read_csv(directory / "foods.csv"):
103	        food = Food(r["namespace"], r["local_id"], r["licence_group"], r["food_group_code"],
104	                    r["food_group_name"], r["source_record"])
105	        if r["food_ref"] != food.food_ref:
106	            raise CanonicalError(f"{directory}/foods.csv: food_ref {r['food_ref']!r} is not "
107	                                 f"namespace:local_id ({food.food_ref!r})")
108	        foods.append(food)
109	    names = [FoodName(r["food_ref"], r["language"], r["name"], r["is_primary"] == "1")
110	             for r in read_csv(directory / "food_names.csv")]
111	    values = [Value(r["food_ref"], r["nutrient_id"], r["basis"], parse_amount(r["amount"]),
112	                    r["qualifier"], r["confidence"], r["source_value"], r["source_nutrient_id"],
113	                    r["source_unit"], r["licence_group"])
114	              for r in read_csv(directory / "values.csv")]
115	    return foods, names, values
116	
117	
118	def read_canonical(directory: Path) -> tuple[list[Food], list[FoodName], list[Value], dict]:
119	    """Reads a row set and refuses it if any file changed after its manifest was written."""
120	    directory = Path(directory)
121	    manifest = read_json(directory / "manifest.json")
122	    for name in ROW_FILES:
123	        actual = sha256_file(directory / name)
124	        if manifest.get("outputs", {}).get(name) != actual:
125	            raise CanonicalError(f"{directory}/{name} does not match its manifest "
126	                                 "(edited after it was written?) — regenerate it")
127	    return (*read_rows(directory), manifest)

1	"""USDA FoodData Central, Foundation Foods — licence group A (CC0 1.0).
2	
3	The reference source module (README "Source rules"): `extract` copies the
4	in-scope rows in USDA's own shape; `canonicalise` applies dictionary/ and
5	nothing else.
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import csv
10	import shutil
11	from collections import defaultdict
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	from ..canonical_io import CanonicalError, write_canonical
15	from ..dictionary import Dictionary
16	from ..lake import (Lake, read_csv, read_json, sha256_file, staged_directory, tool_revision,
17	                    utc_now, write_json)
18	from ..model import Food, FoodName, Value
19	from ..values import NegativeAmount, UnrecognisedValue, convert, qualify, select
20	
21	NAMESPACE = "usda"
22	MANIFEST = "usda"
23	RELEASE_FOLDER = "FoodData_Central_csv_2026-04-30"
24	DATA_TYPES = ("foundation_food",)
25	BASIS = "per_100g"  # FDC reports every nutrient amount per 100 g of food
26	SCOPED_TABLES = ("food.csv", "food_nutrient.csv", "food_portion.csv")
27	WHOLE_TABLES = ("foundation_food.csv", "nutrient.csv", "food_nutrient_derivation.csv",
28	                "food_category.csv", "measure_unit.csv")
29	CANONICAL_INPUTS = ("food.csv", "foundation_food.csv", "food_nutrient.csv", "nutrient.csv",
30	                    "food_nutrient_derivation.csv", "food_category.csv")
31	
32	
33	def _filter_rows(src: Path, dst: Path, keep) -> int:
34	    """Copies the header and every row `keep(row, column_index)` accepts. Cells untouched."""
35	    kept = 0
36	    with open(src, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fin, \
37	            open(dst, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fout:
38	        reader = csv.reader(fin)
39	        writer = csv.writer(fout, lineterminator="\n", quoting=csv.QUOTE_ALL)
40	        header = next(reader)
41	        writer.writerow(header)
42	        column = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(header)}
43	        for row in reader:
44	            if keep(row, column):
45	                writer.writerow(row)
46	                kept += 1
47	    return kept
48	
49	
50	def extract(lake: Lake) -> Path:
51	    inputs = lake.verify_inputs(MANIFEST, [f"{RELEASE_FOLDER}/{t}" for t in SCOPED_TABLES + WHOLE_TABLES])
52	    source = lake.source_dir(MANIFEST) / RELEASE_FOLDER
53	    out = lake.extracted(NAMESPACE)
54	    with staged_directory(out) as scratch:
55	        in_scope: set[str] = set()
56	
57	        def foundation(row, column):
58	            if row[column["data_type"]] in DATA_TYPES:
59	                in_scope.add(row[column["fdc_id"]])
60	                return True
61	            return False
62	
63	        rows = {"food.csv": _filter_rows(source / "food.csv", scratch / "food.csv", foundation)}
64	        for table in SCOPED_TABLES[1:]:
65	            rows[table] = _filter_rows(source / table, scratch / table,
66	                                       lambda row, column: row[column["fdc_id"]] in in_scope)
67	        for table in WHOLE_TABLES:
68	            shutil.copyfile(source / table, scratch / table)
69	        write_json(scratch / "manifest.json", {
70	            "stage": "extract",
71	            "namespace": NAMESPACE,
72	            "release": lake.manifest(MANIFEST)["release"],
73	            "data_types": list(DATA_TYPES),
74	            "generated_at": utc_now(),
75	            "tool_revision": tool_revision(),
76	            "inputs": inputs,
77	            "rows_kept": rows,
78	            "outputs": {p.name: sha256_file(p) for p in sorted(scratch.iterdir())},
79	        })
80	    return out
81	
82	
83	def canonicalise(lake: Lake, dictionary: Dictionary) -> dict:
84	    ext = lake.extracted(NAMESPACE)
85	    extracted = read_json(ext / "manifest.json")
86	    for name in CANONICAL_INPUTS:
87	        if extracted["outputs"].get(name) != sha256_file(ext / name):
88	            raise CanonicalError(f"{ext / name} changed after extraction; re-run `extract usda`")
89	    inputs = [{"file": f"processed/extracted/{NAMESPACE}/{name}", "sha256": extracted["outputs"][name]}
90	              for name in CANONICAL_INPUTS]
91	
92	    group = dictionary.group_of(NAMESPACE)
93	    listed = {r["fdc_id"] for r in read_csv(ext / "foundation_food.csv")}
94	    categories = {r["id"]: r for r in read_csv(ext / "food_category.csv")}
95	    derivation_codes = {r["id"]: r["code"] for r in read_csv(ext / "food_nutrient_derivation.csv")}
96	    units = {r["id"]: r["unit_name"] for r in read_csv(ext / "nutrient.csv")}
97	    mappings = dictionary.mappings_for(NAMESPACE)
98	    for maps in mappings.values():
99	        for m in maps:
100	            if units.get(m.source_nutrient_id) != m.source_unit:
101	                raise CanonicalError(f"nutrient_map.csv gives usda {m.source_nutrient_id} unit "
102	                                     f"{m.source_unit!r}; nutrient.csv says "
103	                                     f"{units.get(m.source_nutrient_id)!r}")
104	    tokens = dictionary.tokens_for(NAMESPACE)
105	    derivations = dictionary.derivations_for(NAMESPACE)
106	
107	    foods: list[Food] = []
108	    names: list[FoodName] = []
109	    excluded: list[dict] = []
110	    for row in read_csv(ext / "food.csv"):
111	        fdc_id = row["fdc_id"]
112	        if fdc_id not in listed:
113	            excluded.append({"fdc_id": fdc_id, "description": row["description"],
114	                             "publication_date": row["publication_date"],
115	                             "reason": "data_type foundation_food but not listed in "
116	                                       "foundation_food.csv (superseded or withdrawn record)"})
117	            continue
118	        category = categories.get(row["food_category_id"], {})
119	        food = Food(NAMESPACE, fdc_id, group, category.get("code", ""),
120	                    category.get("description", ""), f"food.csv fdc_id={fdc_id}")
121	        foods.append(food)
122	        names.append(FoodName(food.food_ref, "en", row["description"].strip(), True))
123	
124	    kept = {f.local_id for f in foods}
125	    mapped = {m.source_nutrient_id for maps in mappings.values() for m in maps}
126	    by_food: dict[str, dict[str, dict]] = defaultdict(dict)
127	    unmapped_duplicates: list[dict] = []
128	    for row in read_csv(ext / "food_nutrient.csv"):
129	        if row["fdc_id"] not in kept:
130	            continue
131	        if row["nutrient_id"] in by_food[row["fdc_id"]]:
132	            if row["nutrient_id"] in mapped:
133	                raise CanonicalError(f"usda:{row['fdc_id']} has two food_nutrient rows for nutrient "
134	                                     f"{row['nutrient_id']}; refusing to pick one")
135	            # Not canonicalised in this phase, so nothing is picked — but a reviewer should know.
136	            unmapped_duplicates.append({"fdc_id": row["fdc_id"], "nutrient_id": row["nutrient_id"],
137	                                        "food_nutrient_ids": [by_food[row["fdc_id"]][row["nutrient_id"]]["id"],
138	                                                              row["id"]]})
139	            continue
140	        by_food[row["fdc_id"]][row["nutrient_id"]] = row
141	
142	    values: list[Value] = []
143	    rejected: list[dict] = []
144	    for food in foods:
145	        published = by_food.get(food.local_id, {})
146	        for nutrient_id, maps in mappings.items():
147	            candidates = []
148	            for m in maps:
149	                row = published.get(m.source_nutrient_id)
150	                if row is None or not row["amount"].strip():
151	                    continue
152	                code = derivation_codes.get(row["derivation_id"]) if row["derivation_id"] else ""
153	                if code is None:
154	                    raise CanonicalError(f"{food.food_ref}: derivation_id {row['derivation_id']!r} "
155	                                         "is not in food_nutrient_derivation.csv")
156	                if code not in derivations:
157	                    raise CanonicalError(f"USDA derivation code {code!r} has no row in "
158	                                         "dictionary/derivation_qualifiers.csv")
159	                try:
160	                    qualified = qualify(row["amount"], tokens=tokens,
161	                                        numeric_override=m.numeric_qualifier_override,
162	                                        derivation_qualifier=derivations[code])
163	                except NegativeAmount:
164	                    # USDA publishes a negative "carbohydrate, by difference" where the other
165	                    # proximates sum past 100 g. Not a quantity: no row, and it is recorded.
166	                    rejected.append({"food_ref": food.food_ref, "source_nutrient_id": m.source_nutrient_id,
167	                                     "source_value": row["amount"], "reason": "negative amount"})
168	                    continue
169	                except UnrecognisedValue as error:
170	                    raise CanonicalError(f"{food.food_ref} nutrient {m.source_nutrient_id}: {error}") from error
171	                candidates.append((m.priority, qualified, (m, row, code)))
172	            chosen = select(candidates)
173	            if chosen is None:
174	                continue
175	            _, qualified, (m, row, code) = chosen
176	            values.append(Value(food.food_ref, nutrient_id, BASIS,
177	                                convert(qualified.amount, m.unit_conversion), qualified.qualifier,
178	                                code, row["amount"].strip(), m.source_nutrient_id,
179	                                units[m.source_nutrient_id], group))
180	
181	    return write_canonical(lake.canonical(NAMESPACE), namespace=NAMESPACE, foods=foods, names=names,
182	                           values=values, dictionary=dictionary, inputs=inputs,
183	                           notes={"data_types": list(DATA_TYPES), "excluded": excluded,
184	                                  "rejected_values": rejected,
185	                                  "unmapped_duplicates": unmapped_duplicates})
186

1	"""Source modules. Each defines NAMESPACE, extract(lake) and canonicalise(lake, dictionary).
2	
3	Discovered by name so that adding a source never edits a shared file.

5	from __future__ import annotations

7	import importlib
8	import pkgutil
9	from types import ModuleType

12	def load_sources() -> dict[str, ModuleType]:
13	    found: dict[str, ModuleType] = {}
14	    for info in pkgutil.iter_modules(__path__):
15	        if info.name.startswith("_"):
16	            continue
17	        module = importlib.import_module(f"{__name__}.{info.name}")
18	        found[module.NAMESPACE] = module
19	    return dict(sorted(found.items()))

1	"""python3 -m almanac_nutrition <command> — see ../README.md."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import argparse
5	import json
6	import sys
7	
8	from . import bundle, fixture
9	from .canonical_io import CanonicalError
10	from .dictionary import DictionaryError, load
11	from .lake import InputVerificationError, Lake
12	from .licence import LicenceViolation
13	from .sources import load_sources
14	
15	FAILURES = (CanonicalError, DictionaryError, InputVerificationError, LicenceViolation)
16	
17	
18	def _summary(manifest: dict) -> str:
19	    c = manifest["counts"]
20	    return (f"{c['foods']} foods, {c['names']} names, {c['values']} values; "
21	            f"qualifiers {json.dumps(c['values_by_qualifier'])}")
22	
23	
24	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
25	    sources = load_sources()
26	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="almanac_nutrition", description=__doc__)
27	    parser.add_argument("--lake", help="food-data lake root "
28	                                       "(default: $ALMANAC_FOOD_DATA or ~/ALManac-food-data)")
29	    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
30	    for name in ("extract", "canonicalise"):
31	        commands.add_parser(name).add_argument("source", choices=sorted(sources))
32	    commands.add_parser("union")
33	    commands.add_parser("bundle")
34	    commands.add_parser("all", help="extract and canonicalise every source, then union and bundle")
35	    commands.add_parser("fixture", help="regenerate fixtures/bundle_v1.sql for AlmanacCore's tests")
36	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
37	
38	    lake = Lake(args.lake)
39	    try:
40	        dictionary = load()
41	        if args.command == "extract":
42	            print(f"extracted {args.source} -> {sources[args.source].extract(lake)}")
43	        elif args.command == "canonicalise":
44	            print(f"canonical {args.source}: {_summary(sources[args.source].canonicalise(lake, dictionary))}")
45	        elif args.command == "union":
46	            print(f"union: {_summary(bundle.union(lake, dictionary))}")
47	        elif args.command == "fixture":
48	            print(f"fixture -> {fixture.write(dictionary)}")
49	        elif args.command == "bundle":
50	            report = bundle.build(lake, dictionary)
51	            print(f"bundle {report['path']} ({', '.join(report['namespaces'])}): "
52	                  f"{report['rows_checked']} rows passed the licence assertion; sha256 {report['sha256']}")
53	        else:
54	            for namespace, module in sources.items():
55	                module.extract(lake)
56	                print(f"canonical {namespace}: {_summary(module.canonicalise(lake, dictionary))}")
57	            print(f"union: {_summary(bundle.union(lake, dictionary))}")
58	            report = bundle.build(lake, dictionary)
59	            print(f"bundle {report['path']}: {report['rows_checked']} rows passed the licence "
60	                  f"assertion; sha256 {report['sha256']}")
61	    except FAILURES as error:
62	        print(f"FAILED: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
63	        return 1
64	    return 0

200	
201	Data formats
202	CoFID data are provided as Excel workbooks containing data in worksheets related to
203	nutrient groups.
204	
205	
206	
207	
208	                                                   6
209	 McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods integrated dataset 2021
210	
211	
212	
213	Format of Excel files
214	The Excel workbook consists of the following worksheets:
215	
216	List of worksheets in CoFID 2021
217	Factors
218	Proximates
219	Inorganics
220	Vitamins
221	Vitamin Fractions
222	Saturated fatty acids per 100g fatty acids
223	Saturated fatty acids per 100g food
224	Monounsaturated fatty acids per 100g fatty acids
225	Monounsaturated fatty acids per 100g food
226	Polyunsaturated fatty acids per 100g fatty acids
227	Polyunsaturated fatty acids per 100g food
228	Phytosterols
229	Organic acids
230	
231	Each sheet contains column headings in rows 1 to 3 of the spreadsheet, then data values
232	for each individual foodstuff such that data values for a specific food code will occur in the
233	same row in each of the worksheets.
234	
235	The following notes apply to the data values:
236	
237	Nutrient values are expressed per 100g of the food except in the case of alcoholic
238	beverages which are presented per 100ml.
239	
240	A trace value for a nutrient is represented by Tr.
241	
242	Where a nutrient is present in significant quantities, but there is no reliable information on
243	the amount, the value is represented by N.
244	
245	In the Excel files, it is not possible to append nutrient-specific footnotes. However, these
246	are being updated in the Composition of Foods Integrated Dataset searchable website.
247	Food-specific footnotes do appear in the Excel version.
248	
249	Food identification
250	Food code
251	Food code is a number, up to 6 digits, representing the unique CoFID code representing
252	each food. The 2-digit prefix generally refers to the food codes used within the book
253	supplements relating to specific food groups, for example, 11- for cereals and cereal
254	
255	                                                   7
256	 McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods integrated dataset 2021
257	
258	
259	
260	products, 12- for milk products and eggs, 16- for fish and fish products. For foods where
261	new data have been incorporated into an existing food, a new food code has been given
262	using the prefix for the appropriate supplement. The food codes should not be considered
263	to have any particular significance as the electronic datasets do not relate exactly to book
264	publications, and each food has a unique food code.
265	
266	Food Name (NAME)
267	The food name has been chosen as that most recognisable and descriptive of the food
268	referenced.
269	
270	Description (DESC) Information
271	Description (DESC) Information given under the description describes the nature of the
272	samples taken for analysis. Sources of values derived, either from the literature or by
273	calculation, are also indicated under this heading.
274	
275	Group (GROUP)
276	In these files (but not in the printed publications) a one, 2 or 3 letter code is assigned to
277	every food. The code letter(s) provide identification of the food group and food type to
278	which the food belongs. A full list of the codes and their description is given in Appendix B.
279	
280	Previous (PREV)
281	Assigned to each food which has an earlier food code with different nutrient values
282	associated with it. It is a number, up to 6 digits, indicating previous food codes (4th, 5th or
283	6th edition or a supplement). Some foods may have more than one previous code
284	associated with them.
285	
286	Main data references (COMMENTS)
287	The main data reference indicates the principal report(s) or publication(s) from which the
288	majority of the data for the food code are taken. Values for individual nutrients within each
289	code may be taken from different sources, calculated or estimated from other codes. For
290	foods that do not have an analytical report or literature source that can be referred to as
291	the main data reference, the food description should indicate how the data have been
292	estimated (for example, from manufacturer’s data, calculated from related codes or
293	calculated as a recipe). In some cases, there is a main data reference referring to
294	analytical data and the description indicates that industry data have also been used to
295	update some nutrients, usually sodium, sugars, fats or added minerals and vitamins.
296	
297	
298	
299	
300	                                                   8
301	 McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods integrated dataset 2021
302	
303	
304	
305	
306	Details of nutrient data
307	For a more detailed definition and expression of the nutrients refer to the introductory
308	pages of the seventh summary edition of McCance and Widdowson's The Composition of
309	Foods (1) and of the supplement publications.
310	
311	The more significant points for certain nutrients are provided in the notes below for
312	convenience. For some nutrients, data which is 'old' and were analysed significantly earlier
313	and on a different sample to the bulk of the nutrients are available. These data have not
314	been updated but are the only data available and may be of interest to some users and are
315	available as a separate file. This applies to fibre fractions, fibre analysed by the Southgate
316	method, and sulphur.
317	
318	
319	Factors worksheet
320	Edible conversion factor (EDPOR)
321	Many foods are purchased or served with material that is clearly inedible or material that
322	might be discarded as inedible by some consumers. For the purposes of this dataset
323	‘waste’ encompasses both types of material, which might include, for example:
324	
325	•   outer leaves or stalks of vegetables
326	•   stones, pips or peel of fruit
327	•   nut shells
328	•   fish skin and bone
329	•   meat fat and bones
330	•   liquid content of canned foods
331	
332	The edible conversion factor allows calculation of the nutrient content of foods when the
333	inedible material is included in the weight and refers to the proportion of edible material
334	remaining after the waste has been removed. The factor will vary between different
335	samples of the same food and these values should be treated as a guide to the typical
336	proportion of inedible waste. In the dataset foods containing inedible portions always have
337	‘weighed with’ in their name.
338	
339	Specific gravity (SPECGRAV)
340	Specific gravity is the ratio of the density (mass of a unit volume) of a food to the density
341	(mass of the same unit volume) of water.
342	
343	Nitrogen conversion factor (NCF)
344	Nitrogen conversion factor is the factor used to calculate protein from total nitrogen. See
345	Protein.
346	
347	Glycerol conversion factor (GCF)
348	
349	                                                   9
350	 McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods integrated dataset 2021
351	
352	
353	
354	Glycerol conversion factor is used to allow the calculation of the total fatty acids in a given
355	weight of food. See Fatty acids.
356	
357	
358	Proximates worksheet
359	Water (WATER)
360	For most foods, water has been analysed using gravimetric methods. In some cases
361	where protein, fat or carbohydrate have been updated based on industry data, the water
362	value has been estimated by calculation (100 – (protein + fat + available carbohydrate +
363	dietary fibre + ash)).
364	
365	Protein (PROT)
366	For most foods, protein is calculated by multiplying total nitrogen values (TOTNIT) by the
367	factors provided in the ‘Nitrogen conversion factor’ column of the ‘Factors’ worksheet, as
368	described in the introduction of McCance and Widdowson's The Composition of Foods
369	seventh summary edition. Unless stated otherwise, a factor of 6.25 is used based on the
370	assumption that proteins contain 16% nitrogen. The proportion of non-protein nitrogen is
371	high in many foods, notably fish, fruits and vegetables. In most of these, however, this is
372	amino acid in nature and therefore little error is involved in the use of a factor applied to
373	the total nitrogen, although protein in the strictest sense is overestimated. For those foods
374	which contain a measurable amount of non-protein nitrogen in the form of urea, purines
375	and pyrimidines (for example, mushrooms) the non-protein nitrogen has been subtracted
376	before multiplication by the appropriate factor.
377	
378	Fat (FAT)
379	The fat in most foods is a mixture of triglycerides, phospholipids, sterols and related
380	compounds. The values in the tables refer to total fat and not just to triglycerides.
381	
382	Carbohydrate (CHO)
383	Total carbohydrate and its components, starch, total and individual sugars (glucose,
384	galactose, fructose, sucrose, maltose, lactose) and oligosaccharides, but not fibre, are
385	wherever possible expressed as their monosaccharide equivalent. The values for total
386	carbohydrate in the dataset have generally been obtained from the sum of analysed
387	values for these components of ‘available carbohydrate’, contrasting with figures for
388	carbohydrate ‘by difference’, which are sometimes used in other food tables or on the
389	labels of processed foods. Such figures are obtained by subtracting the measured weights
390	of the other proximates from the total weight and many include the contribution from any
391	dietary fibre present, as well as errors from the other analyses.
392	
393	Energy value (KCALS)
394	Calculated using the conversion factors: protein 4 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g, carbohydrate
395	(available, expressed as monosaccharides) 3.75 kcal/g and alcohol 7 kcal/g.
396	
397	Energy value (KJ)
398	
399	                                                  10
400	 McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods integrated dataset 2021
401	
402	
403	
404	Calculated using the conversion factors: protein 17 kJ/g, fat 37 kJ/g, carbohydrate
405	(available, expressed as monosaccharides) 16 kJ/g and alcohol 29 kJ/g.
406	
407	Starch (STAR)
408	Includes dextrins but excludes resistant starch. Expressed as monosaccharide
409	equivalents.
410	
411	Oligosaccharides (OLIGO)
412	Expressed as monosaccharide equivalents. Any known or measured contribution from
413	oligosaccharides and/or maltodextrins has been included in the total carbohydrate value
414	but not in the columns for starch or total sugars. In most foods oligosaccharides are
415	present in relatively low quantities. In vegetables and some processed foods where
416	glucose syrups and maltodextrins are added, oligosaccharides will make a significant
417	contribution to carbohydrate content. Where oligosaccharides are present in foods, they
418	are not always measured separately and may be included in the starch, sugar or fibre
419	fractions, depending on the nature of the oligosaccharide and on the analytical methods
420	used.
421	
422	Total sugars (TOTSUG)
423	Sugars are expressed as monosaccharide equivalents and include free monosaccharides
424	(glucose, fructose and galactose) and disaccharides (sucrose, maltose and lactose). The
425	value does not include any contribution from oligosaccharides present in the food.
426	
427	Alcohol (ALCO)
428	Values are given as g/100 ml. Pure ethyl alcohol has a specific gravity of 0.79, dividing
429	values by 0.79 converts them to alcohol by volume (ml/100 ml).
430	
431	NSP (ENGFIB)
432	Non-starch polysaccharides (2) includes insoluble fibre (cellulose, insoluble non-cellulosic
433	polysaccharides) and soluble fibre (soluble cellulosic polysaccharides).
434	
435	AOAC fibre (AOACFIB)
436	AOAC determinations (3) include resistant starch and lignin in the estimation of total fibre,
437	rather than only the non-starch polysaccharides.
438	
439	Fatty acids

import openpyxl, collections, re

MAPPED = ["KCALS", "PROT", "FAT", "CHO", "AOACFIB", "ALCO"]
print({m: idx.get(m) for m in MAPPED})

data = rows[3:]
with_code = [(n, r) for n, r in enumerate(data, start=4) if r[0] is not None and str(r[0]).strip() != ""]
without = [(n, r) for n, r in enumerate(data, start=4) if not (r[0] is not None and str(r[0]).strip() != "")]
print("rows with code:", len(with_code), "without:", len(without))
for n, r in without[:5]:
    print("  no code row", n, r[:8])
print("code types:", collections.Counter(type(r[0]).__name__ for _, r in with_code))
print("codes untrimmed:", [(n, r[0]) for n, r in with_code if isinstance(r[0], str) and r[0] != r[0].strip()][:10])
codes = collections.Counter(str(r[0]).strip() for _, r in with_code)
print("distinct codes:", len(codes))

print("groups untrimmed/empty:", [(n, repr(r[3])) for n, r in with_code if not isinstance(r[3], str) or r[3] != r[3].strip() or not r[3]][:20])
groups = collections.Counter(r[3] for _, r in with_code)
print("groups:", sorted(groups.items()))
# mapped profile
all_profile = collections.Counter()
for m in MAPPED:
    prof = collections.Counter()
    others = collections.Counter()
    for n, r in with_code:
        c = r[idx[m]]
        if c is None:
            prof["blank(None)"] += 1
        elif isinstance(c, str):
            s = c.strip()
            if s == "":
                prof["blank(str)"] += 1
            elif s in ("Tr", "N"):
                prof[s] += 1
            elif re.fullmatch(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?", s):
                prof["numeric str"] += 1
                if float(s) == 0: prof["zero str"] += 1
                if float(s) < 0: prof["negative str"] += 1
                if s != c: prof["untrimmed numeric"] += 1
            else:
                others[c] += 1
        elif isinstance(c, (int, float)):
            prof[type(c).__name__] += 1
            if c == 0: prof["zero num"] += 1
            if c < 0: prof["negative num"] += 1
        else:
            others[repr(c)] += 1
    print(m, dict(prof), "OTHER:", dict(others))
# whole-sheet tokens in all data columns
tok = collections.Counter()
for n, r in with_code:
    for c in r[7:]:
        if c is None: tok["None"] += 1
        elif isinstance(c, str):
            s = c.strip()
            if s in ("Tr", "N"): tok[s] += 1
            elif s == "": tok["emptystr"] += 1
            elif re.fullmatch(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)", s): tok["num-str"] += 1
            else: tok["other:" + c] += 1
        else: tok[type(c).__name__] += 1
print("1.3 all data cols:", dict(tok))
# numeric cells in mapped columns examples
ex = [(n, m, r[idx[m]]) for n, r in with_code for m in MAPPED if isinstance(r[idx[m]], (int, float))]
print("numeric-typed mapped cells examples:", ex[:10], len(ex))

def sheet_file(workbook: str, title: str) -> str:
    """The extracted CSV for one sheet: `<workbook stem>__<sheet title, sanitised>.csv`."""
    return f"{Path(workbook).stem}__{re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9.-]+', '_', title).strip('_')}.csv"


def cell_text(value: object, where: str) -> str:
    """One XLSX cell as a string, unparsed: text as-is, numbers as their shortest round trip."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, float):
        return repr(value)
    if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool):
        return str(value)
    # Dates, booleans, errors: nothing in CoFID 2021 has one, so none is guessed at.
    raise CanonicalError(f"{where}: cell of type {type(value).__name__} ({value!r}) has no "
                         "verbatim text form; refusing to extract it")


def basis_of(food_group_code: str) -> str:
    return "per_100ml" if food_group_code.startswith(ALCOHOLIC_GROUP_PREFIX) else "per_100g"


def extract(lake: Lake) -> Path:
    inputs = lake.verify_inputs(MANIFEST, INPUTS)
    source = lake.source_dir(MANIFEST)
    out = lake.extracted(NAMESPACE)
    with staged_directory(out) as scratch:
        sheets = []
        for workbook in INPUTS:
            book = openpyxl.load_workbook(source / workbook, read_only=True, data_only=True)
            try:
                for sheet in book.worksheets:
                    name = sheet_file(workbook, sheet.title)
                    if (scratch / name).exists():
                        raise CanonicalError(f"{workbook}: sheet {sheet.title!r} and another sheet "
                                             f"both extract to {name}")
                    rows = columns = 0
                    with open(scratch / name, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        writer = csv.writer(f, lineterminator="\n", quoting=csv.QUOTE_ALL)
                        for rows, row in enumerate(sheet.iter_rows(values_only=True), start=1):
                            writer.writerow([cell_text(v, f"{workbook}!{sheet.title} row {rows}")
                                             for v in row])
                            columns = max(columns, len(row))
                    sheets.append({"workbook": workbook, "sheet": sheet.title, "file": name,
                                   "rows": rows, "columns": columns})
            finally:
                book.close()
        write_json(scratch / "manifest.json", {
            "stage": "extract",
            "namespace": NAMESPACE,
            "release": lake.manifest(MANIFEST)["release"],
            "generated_at": utc_now(),
            "tool_revision": tool_revision(),
            "inputs": inputs,
            "sheets": sheets,
            "outputs": {p.name: sha256_file(p) for p in sorted(scratch.iterdir())},
        })
    return out


def _read_food_sheet(lake: Lake) -> tuple[list[list[str]], list[dict]]:
    ext = lake.extracted(NAMESPACE)
    name = sheet_file(WORKBOOK, FOOD_SHEET)
    if not (ext / "manifest.json").is_file() or not (ext / name).is_file():
        raise CanonicalError(f"{ext / name} is missing; run `extract {NAMESPACE}` first")
    recorded = read_json(ext / "manifest.json").get("outputs", {}).get(name)
    if recorded != sha256_file(ext / name):
        raise CanonicalError(f"{ext / name} changed after extraction; re-run `extract {NAMESPACE}`")
    with open(ext / name, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    if len(rows) < HEADER_ROWS:
        raise CanonicalError(f"{FOOD_SHEET}: {len(rows)} rows, fewer than its {HEADER_ROWS} header rows")
    return rows, [{"file": f"processed/extracted/{NAMESPACE}/{name}", "sha256": recorded}]


def _column(cells: list[str], text: str, where: str) -> int:
    found = [i for i, cell in enumerate(cells) if cell.strip() == text]
    if len(found) != 1:
        raise CanonicalError(f"{FOOD_SHEET} {where}: {text!r} is in {len(found)} columns, expected 1")
    return found[0]


def canonicalise(lake: Lake, dictionary: Dictionary) -> dict:
    rows, inputs = _read_food_sheet(lake)
    headings, codes = rows[0], rows[CODE_ROW - 1]
    code_col = _column(headings, FOOD_CODE, "row 1")
    name_col = _column(headings, FOOD_NAME, "row 1")
    group_col = _column(headings, GROUP, "row 1")

    group = dictionary.group_of(NAMESPACE)
    tokens = dictionary.tokens_for(NAMESPACE)
    mappings = dictionary.mappings_for(NAMESPACE)
    columns: dict[str, int] = {}
    for maps in mappings.values():
        for m in maps:
            col = _column(codes, m.source_nutrient_id, f"row {CODE_ROW} (nutrient codes)")
            if not headings[col].strip().endswith(f"({m.source_unit})"):
                raise CanonicalError(f"nutrient_map.csv gives {NAMESPACE} {m.source_nutrient_id} unit "
                                     f"{m.source_unit!r}; {FOOD_SHEET} row 1 says {headings[col]!r}")
            columns[m.source_nutrient_id] = col

    def cell(row: list[str], col: int) -> str:
        return row[col] if col < len(row) else ""

    body = list(enumerate(rows[HEADER_ROWS:], start=HEADER_ROWS + 1))
    coded = [(n, row) for n, row in body if cell(row, code_col).strip()]
    excluded = [{"row": n, "cells": [c for c in row if c.strip()],
                 "reason": f"no {FOOD_CODE}; README takes foods from rows with one"}
                for n, row in body if not cell(row, code_col).strip() and any(c.strip() for c in row)]
    occurrences = Counter(cell(row, code_col).strip() for _, row in coded)

    foods: list[tuple[Food, int, list[str]]] = []
    names: list[FoodName] = []
    collisions: dict[str, dict] = {}
    unlisted_groups: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for n, row in coded:
        code = cell(row, code_col).strip()
        local_id = code
        if occurrences[code] > 1:
            # README: every occurrence of a repeated publisher code becomes {code}@row{n}.
            local_id = f"{code}@row{n}"
            entry = collisions.setdefault(code, {"food_code": code, "rows": [], "local_ids": [],
                                                 "names": []})
            entry["rows"].append(n)
            entry["local_ids"].append(local_id)
            entry["names"].append(cell(row, name_col).strip())
        group_code = cell(row, group_col).strip()
        if group_code not in APPENDIX_B:
            unlisted_groups.setdefault(group_code, []).append(f"{NAMESPACE}:{local_id}")
        food = Food(NAMESPACE, local_id, group, group_code, APPENDIX_B.get(group_code, ""),
                    f"{FOOD_SHEET}!row {n}")
        foods.append((food, n, row))
        names.append(FoodName(food.food_ref, "en", cell(row, name_col).strip(), True))

    values: list[Value] = []
    rejected: list[dict] = []
    for food, n, row in foods:
        basis = basis_of(food.food_group_code)
        for nutrient_id, maps in mappings.items():
            candidates = []
            for m in maps:
                text = cell(row, columns[m.source_nutrient_id])
                if not text.strip():
                    continue  # blank: CoFID says nothing, so there is no row
                try:
                    qualified = qualify(text, tokens=tokens, numeric_override=m.numeric_qualifier_override)
                except NegativeAmount:
                    rejected.append({"food_ref": food.food_ref, "source_nutrient_id": m.source_nutrient_id,
                                     "source_value": text.strip(), "reason": "negative amount"})
                    continue
                except UnrecognisedValue as error:
                    raise CanonicalError(f"{food.food_ref} ({FOOD_SHEET}!row {n}) "
                                         f"{m.source_nutrient_id}: {error}") from error
                candidates.append((m.priority, qualified, (m, text.strip())))
            chosen = select(candidates)
            if chosen is None:
                continue
            _, qualified, (m, source_value) = chosen
            values.append(Value(food.food_ref, nutrient_id, basis,
                                convert(qualified.amount, m.unit_conversion), qualified.qualifier,
                                "", source_value, m.source_nutrient_id, m.source_unit, group))

    by_ref = {food.food_ref: (food, names[i].name) for i, (food, _, _) in enumerate(foods)}
    notes = {
        "sheet": FOOD_SHEET,
        "not_canonicalised": [f"{WORKBOOK}: every sheet but {FOOD_SHEET}",
                              f"{OLD_FOODS}: every sheet (superseded analyses)"],
        "basis_rule": f"per_100ml for food groups starting {ALCOHOLIC_GROUP_PREFIX!r} (alcoholic "
                      "beverages: user guide p.7, sheet 1.1 Notes); per_100g for every other food",
        "per_100ml_foods": [{"food_ref": f.food_ref, "food_group_code": f.food_group_code,
                             "name": by_ref[f.food_ref][1]}
                            for f, _, _ in foods if basis_of(f.food_group_code) == "per_100ml"],
        # Alcohol in a food outside group Q: per_100g by the rule above. Listed so that a
        # reviewer can see every such food (dishes cooked with wine, and Irish coffee).
        "alcohol_outside_alcoholic_groups": [
            {"food_ref": v.food_ref, "food_group_code": by_ref[v.food_ref][0].food_group_code,
             "name": by_ref[v.food_ref][1], "source_value": v.source_value, "basis": v.basis}
            for v in values if v.nutrient_id == "alcohol" and v.amount and v.basis == "per_100g"],
        "food_group_names": f"user guide {GUIDE} (sha256 {GUIDE_SHA256}) Appendix B",
        "food_groups_not_in_appendix_b": unlisted_groups,
        "collisions": list(collisions.values()),
        "excluded": excluded,
        "rejected_values": rejected,
    }
    return write_canonical(lake.canonical(NAMESPACE), namespace=NAMESPACE,
                           foods=[food for food, _, _ in foods], names=names, values=values,
                           dictionary=dictionary, inputs=inputs, notes=notes)

FOOD_CODE, FOOD_NAME, GROUP = "Food Code", "Food Name", "Group"

# QG vermouths, QI liqueurs, QK spirits, and Q itself (pre-mixed drinks).
